{{Short description|Analysis tool used to find the approximate error in a result}}
{{Other uses|Residual (disambiguation){{!}}Residual}}

Loosely speaking, a '''residual''' is the [[Error#Experimental_science|error]] in a result.<ref>{{cite web |first=Jonathan Richard |last=Shewchuk |url=https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake-papers/painless-conjugate-gradient.pdf#page=12 |title=An Introduction to the Conjugate Gradient Method Without the Agonizing Pain |page=6 |date=1994 }}</ref> To be precise, suppose we want to find ''x'' such that 

: <math>f(x)=b.</math>

Given an approximation ''x''<sub>0</sub> of ''x'', the residual is 

: <math>b - f(x_0)</math>

that is, "what is left of the right hand side" after subtracting ''f''(''x''<sub>0</sub>)" (thus, the name "residual": what is left, the rest). On the other hand, the error is

: <math>x - x_0</math>

If the exact value of ''x'' is not known, the residual can be computed, whereas the error cannot.

==Residual of the approximation of a function==
Similar terminology is used dealing with [[differential equation|differential]], [[integral equation|integral]] and [[functional equation]]s. For the approximation <math>f_\text{a}</math> of the solution <math>f</math> of the equation
:<math> T(f)(x)=g(x) \, ,</math>
the residual can either be the function
: <math>~g(x)~ - ~T(f_\text{a})(x)</math>,
or can be said to be the maximum of the norm of this difference
: <math>\max_{x\in \mathcal X} |g(x)-T(f_\text{a})(x)| </math>
over the domain <math>\mathcal X</math>, where the function <math>f_\text{a}</math> is expected to approximate the solution <math> f </math>,

or some integral of a function of the difference, for example:

: <math>\int_{\mathcal X} |g(x)-T(f_\text{a})(x)|^2~ \mathrm dx.</math>

In many cases, the smallness of the residual means that the approximation is close to the solution, i.e., 

: <math>\left|\frac{f_\text{a}(x) - f(x)}{f(x)}\right| \ll  1.</math>

In these cases, the initial equation is considered as [[well-posed]]; and the residual can be considered as a measure of deviation of the approximation from the exact solution.

==Use of residuals==

When one does not know the exact solution, one may look for the approximation with small residual.

Residuals appear in many areas in mathematics, including [[iterative solver]]s such as the [[generalized minimal residual method]], which seeks solutions to equations by systematically minimizing the residual. In [[physics-informed neural networks]], an additional term is included in the [[loss function]] consisting of the residual of the [[Partial differential equation|PDE]].
